hrv_below_personal_baseline.title: Microgravity alters respiratory sinus arrhythmia and short-term heart rate variability in humans
hrv_below_personal_baseline.plain_words: In a NASA-indexed study of four crew on a 16-day flight, heart rate variability linked to the body's calming (vagal) control fell after the flight and stayed changed for at least 15 days.
hrv_below_personal_baseline.key_finding: fell after the flight and stayed changed for at least 15 days
hrv_below_personal_baseline.countermeasure: Do the planned ARED or T2 exercise session today.
hrv_below_personal_baseline.countermeasure_source: NTRS 20140002864, Benefits, Consequences, and Uncertainties of Conventional (Exercise) Countermeasure Approaches, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20140002864

heart_rate_above_personal_baseline.title: Microgravity alters respiratory sinus arrhythmia and short-term heart rate variability in humans
heart_rate_above_personal_baseline.plain_words: In the same study, heart rate rose about 15 percent right after landing and was still raised 15 days later.
heart_rate_above_personal_baseline.key_finding: heart rate rose about 15 percent right after landing
heart_rate_above_personal_baseline.countermeasure: Repeat the reading at rest; if it is still high, report to the flight surgeon today.
heart_rate_above_personal_baseline.countermeasure_source: to be confirmed by research lead

sleep_below_personal_baseline.title: Impact of Sleep Shifting Strategies on the International Space Station
sleep_below_personal_baseline.plain_words: Wrist-worn sleep records from 19 ISS crew show that schedule disruptions such as visiting vehicles cut sleep into short blocks; earlier crews averaged about six hours a night.
sleep_below_personal_baseline.key_finding: schedule disruptions such as visiting vehicles cut sleep into short blocks
sleep_below_personal_baseline.countermeasure: Check the sleep space: cool, dark, quiet and private, with the crew quarters set to your own preference.
sleep_below_personal_baseline.countermeasure_source: NTRS 20190002002, Sleep Environment Recommendations for Future Spaceflight Vehicles, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20190002002

reaction_above_personal_baseline.title: Cognitive Performance in ISS Astronauts on 6-Month Low Earth Orbit Missions
reaction_above_personal_baseline.plain_words: NASA tested 25 astronauts before, during and after 6-month ISS missions and found processing speed and sustained attention slowed early in flight.
reaction_above_personal_baseline.key_finding: processing speed and sustained attention slowed early in flight
reaction_above_personal_baseline.countermeasure: Keep to the planned sleep window tonight and to the station's circadian lighting schedule.
reaction_above_personal_baseline.countermeasure_source: NTRS 20240002094, Impact of Sleep Shifting Strategies on the International Space Station, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20240002094; NTRS 20140012988, Addressing Challenges to the Design & Test of Operational Lighting Environments for the International Space Station, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20140012988

mood_below_personal_baseline.title: Dynamic nature of epigenetic patterns observed during the Mars 520-d mission simulation
mood_below_personal_baseline.plain_words: In a 520-day simulated mission to Mars, researchers followed the mood state of 6 crew members over time and linked changes in it to the long isolation.
mood_below_personal_baseline.key_finding: linked changes in it to the long isolation
mood_below_personal_baseline.countermeasure: Use tonight's scheduled private conference or crew journal entry; tell the flight surgeon if mood stays low tomorrow.
mood_below_personal_baseline.countermeasure_source: to be confirmed by research lead

two_signals_in_48h.title: Dynamic nature of epigenetic patterns observed during the Mars 520-d mission simulation
two_signals_in_48h.plain_words: In a 520-day simulated mission to Mars, researchers profiled mood state, biochemistry and DNA methylation together in 6 crew members and reported that changes in these measures were related to one another during the isolation.
two_signals_in_48h.key_finding: changes in these measures were related to one another
two_signals_in_48h.countermeasure: Do the planned ARED or T2 exercise session today.
two_signals_in_48h.countermeasure_source: NTRS 20140002864, Benefits, Consequences, and Uncertainties of Conventional (Exercise) Countermeasure Approaches, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20140002864

spo2_below_personal_baseline.countermeasure: Check the sensor fit and repeat the reading; if still low, report to the flight surgeon today.
spo2_below_personal_baseline.countermeasure_source: to be confirmed by research lead

core_temp_above_personal_baseline.countermeasure: Reduce exercise load today, keep to the scheduled fluid intake, and repeat the reading later today.
core_temp_above_personal_baseline.countermeasure_source: to be confirmed by research lead
